subject: Copywriting
title: The Science of Stickiness
description: A fast breakdown of The Science of Stickiness for builders.

hook.text: Why do you remember 'Just Do It' but forget thousands of other slogans?

buildup.text: The Science of Stickiness sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: Sticky slogans hit at least three: 'Think Different' is simple, unexpected, and emotional. That's why it endures.

twist.text: Clever slogans often fail the stickiness test. Puns are forgettable. Simplicity and emotion outlast wordplay every time.

climax.text: The stickiest slogans become part of the language itself. 'Where's the beef?' entered everyday speech.

punchline.text: Simple, unexpected, emotional. Three traits of slogans that stick.

quiz.question: What are the six principles of 'sticky' ideas?
options: Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, Story
Fast, Loud, Visual, Funny, Short, Clever
Bold, Bright, Big, Brave, Brief, Beautiful

details.summary: Sticky slogans share identifiable traits: simplicity, unexpectedness, concreteness, credibility, emotion, and story. Chip and Dan Heath's SUCCESs framework explains why some ideas survive while others vanish. The stickiest slogans activate multiple elements at once.
details.whyItMatters: Stickiness is not random luck — it follows patterns that can be learned. Understanding what makes ideas stick transforms slogan writing from guesswork into a repeatable craft.
takeaways: Sticky messages share six key traits from the SUCCESs framework
Unexpectedness breaks mental patterns and demands attention
Concrete imagery is remembered far better than abstract claims

faq.question: What is the SUCCESs framework for sticky messages?
faq.answer: Developed by Chip and Dan Heath, SUCCESs stands for Simple, Unexpected, Concrete, Credible, Emotional, and Stories. Messages that incorporate several of these elements are far more likely to be remembered and shared.

faq.question: Why do some slogans stick while others are forgotten?
faq.answer: Forgotten slogans tend to be abstract, generic, or predictable. Sticky slogans surprise us, use vivid imagery, and connect to something we already care about. 'Got Milk?' works because it is unexpected, concrete, and emotionally relatable.
